steps.what: Make announcements regarding flights using the public address system

tasks.design: Retain pilot announcements through {OTHER}, the aircraft public address system. Test existing approved announcement facilities before proposing a separate tool; a passenger question-answering case does not establish savings in pilot communication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Announcement content and timing depend on the actual flight situation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing announcement facilities support communication without proving reduced pilot time.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining uncertainty clearly and choosing an appropriate moment to speak.

evidence.claim: The KLM case describes reviewed AI answers to social-media inquiries, not automated pilot public-address announcements.
Pilot announcement time is retained because no separate repetitive preparation burden is established.

assumptions: Boundary is pilot announcement preparation within delivery and speaking, excluding cabin crew's separate passenger work.
Pilot establishes current flight context and confirms relevant crew information during s1; no machine is supplied a free flight-event trigger or approved announcement text.
OTHER is the aircraft public address system. Existing native announcement facilities are checked first if a repeated burden is observed.
No new tool or capture requirement means zero incremental upkeep.
research_questions: Is any repeated announcement preparation separable from situational communication?

steps.what: Check the instrument flight plan and filing details in the existing planning system
File the checked instrument flight plan and resolve acknowledgement or rejection messages

tasks.design: Use the existing native filing route in {OTHER}, the aviation planning and filing system, while retaining version checking and response handling. Check native configuration first; already automated transmission and plan preparation do not create a new pilot labour saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Filing requires correct flight details and handling of system responses.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital planning exists, but that alone does not establish additional manual filing effort to remove.
tasks.still_hard: Rejects and changes require checking the exact plan version and current flight context.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a filing response requires operational clarification.
tasks.altitude: Filing accountability and operational judgement remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Flight plan versioning and acknowledgement status

evidence.claim: Lido Flight 4D supports digital flight planning against weather and airspace restrictions; this capability does not establish local pilot filing savings.
Existing transmission runtime is excluded from human savings; checking and response resolution remain counted.

assumptions: Boundary is pilot filing where assigned, not dispatcher plan construction, flight-plan review elsewhere, ATC coordination or flight execution. Dispatcher-filed flights add no pilot filing saving.

Flight planning staff or the pilot's separate planning task produce the prepared plan before s1. Pilot checks flight ID, aircraft identity/type/equipment, dates/times, aerodromes, route/levels and every required filing field against the system's current specification within s1; missing fields return to the responsible planner manually.

The filing service produces acknowledgements or rejects only after submission during s2; response handling time remains fully counted and is not assumed ready beforehand. Amendments are checked again before further submission.
Native filing is already the first option. No new interface or capture obligation means zero incremental upkeep.
research_questions: Is any duplicate pilot transcription left after native filing and dispatcher responsibilities are accounted for?

tasks.enabler_now: Electronic technical logs support reporting but do not replace maintenance work.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding the issue and making a clear handoff to qualified maintenance staff.
tasks.human_edge: Accurate observation and communication of what happened on the aircraft.
tasks.altitude: Maintenance observation and handoff responsibility remain unchanged.

assumptions: Boundary includes only pilot work where permitted and maintenance arrangement, excluding maintenance engineers' work, aircraft release and separate log-recording tasks.

OTHER is the technical log system. Native log functions are checked first if a distinct reporting burden emerges.
